newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - May 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - May 5.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Monday:
* Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko said at a meeting with rebel leader Laurent Kabila that he would give up power, but only to a transitional authority who would organize national elections.
* The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation said evidence from an investigation into the cause of the crash of Trans World Airlines flight 800 indicated a "catastrophic mechanical failure".
* Several of the United States have outlawed so-called "partial birth abortions", and other states are also considering doing so, while Congress again tries to ban the procedure.
* According to documents and interviews, two of President Bill Clinton's closest confidants knew of Webster Hubbell's serious troubles before he resigned as Associate Attorney General in March 1994.

* A man paralyzed by a fall off a power pole in 1962 is still trying to obtain workers' compensation benefits. Utilities Mutual Insurance Co, the workers' compensation insurer for the man's former employer, Niagara Mohawk Power Corp, says it has no obligation to pay until appeals are over.
* Ceferino Jimenez Malla, a Spanish horse trader killed by a firing squad during the Spanish Civil War, became the first gypsy to be beatified by the Roman Catholic Church.
* The man accused of killing Megan Kanka goes on trial in Trenton, New Jersey. The case gave rise to U.S. laws requiring notification when sex offenders move into a neighborhood.
